activity_context.topic_title: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at a General Point

feedback.worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}+36y-16{x}^{2}+32x-124 & =0 \\ 9({y}^{2}+4y)-16({x}^{2}-2x)-124 & =0 \\ 9\,[(y+2)^{2}-4]-16\,[(x-1)^{2}-1]-124 & =0 \\ 9(y+2)^{2}-36-16(x-1)^{2}+16-124 & =0 \\ 9(y+2)^{2}-16(x-1)^{2} & =144 \\ \frac{9(y+2)^{2}}{144}-\frac{16(x-1)^{2}}{144} & =1 \\ \frac{(y+2)^{2}}{16}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of a vertical hyperbola

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{a}{b}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k)=(1,-2),\,a=\sqrt{16}=4,\,b=\sqrt{9}=3.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-2) & =\pm (\frac{4}{3})(x-1) \\ y+2 & =\pm \,\frac{4}{3}(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$
